title: Air-fryer cheese toastie
subtitle: A melted cheese sandwich, golden and crisp from the air fryer.
excerpt: Two slices of white bread filled with cheddar and toasted in the air fryer until the bread is golden and crisp and the cheese is fully melted. Ready in 8 minutes. Serves one.
sourceNotes: The toasted cheese sandwich (cheese toastie) is a staple of British home cooking. The air fryer produces a uniformly golden, crisp exterior with fully melted cheese inside without the need to watch it in a pan.

content.text: A cheese toastie in the air fryer takes 8 minutes and needs one thing: a light coating of butter or oil on the outer faces of both slices. Without it, the bread dries out rather than toasting golden. The sandwich does not need pressing or turning in the first few minutes ,  wait until the bottom slice has set before flipping.

Butter the outside face of both slices of {{bread-white}} with {{unsalted-butter}} of butter. Place {{cheddar}} of grated or sliced cheddar on the unbuttered side of one slice and sandwich with the other, buttered side out. Preheat the air fryer to 180°C. Place the sandwich in the basket. Cook for 4 minutes, flip carefully using a spatula, and cook for a further 3-4 minutes until both sides are golden and the cheese is fully melted.

items.symptom: Bread drying out and hard rather than golden
items.cause: No fat on the outer surface.
items.fix: The butter or oil on the outside is not optional. Without it the bread dehydrates in the hot air rather than toasting.

items.cause: Cheese not melted enough to act as glue, or moved too soon.
items.fix: Wait the full 4 minutes before flipping. The melted cheese will have sealed the sandwich by then.
Cook at 180°C. Higher temperatures char the bread before the heat reaches the cheese at the centre.

content.text: An air-fryer cheese toastie is a quick lunch. Good with a bowl of tomato soup or a small salad. Add a thin layer of English mustard or chutney to the inside before cooking, or include a few slices of ham or tomato alongside the cheese.
